In an in-depth interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman responded to the company's recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop app and discussed plans for a future tabless interface. The full interview can be watched below.

In the future, work could be completed seamlessly within ChatGPT

A few days ago, Joanna Stern first released a preview clip of her interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her brand-new YouTube channel, New Things.

Stern published the full interview today, covering the new ChatGPT Voice, OpenAI's hardware development plans, the lawsuit with Apple, and the earlier data breach incident at Hugging Face.

During the interview, Stern mentioned that OpenAI had previously decided to merge the ChatGPT and Codex desktop apps and launch a new agent mode called Work.

The merged interface caused considerable confusion, especially among users who simply wanted to continue using ChatGPT but struggled to find their conversation history.

OpenAI subsequently updated the app, adding separate Work and Chat tabs at the top of the interface, along with a dropdown menu in the sidebar to switch between ChatGPT and Codex. Although it is no longer as difficult to use as before, the interface remains somewhat complex.

When asked about this misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern's description of the new interface as "a bit confusing" and added that this is a "transitional arrangement" toward the future, with the Work tab eventually disappearing and its functions being "seamlessly integrated into ChatGPT."

Brockman also stated that despite the confusing rollout of the merged app, OpenAI had achieved its expected results, with the number of Codex users rapidly increasing from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.

When pressed on whether the growth was purely due to cramming Codex into the ChatGPT app, Brockman acknowledged this again, but argued that to some extent, it was also part of the plan:

The entire interview is excellent and absolutely worth watching. It also features a segment very much in Joanna Stern's style, attempting to bring ChatGPT Voice into the conversation—and the results are exactly as you might imagine.
